title: RAW UNREVIEWED: independently completed production booklets isolate metatext from subject vocabulary
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. If separately made units have independently documented completion devices such as a ruled terminal panel or explicit scribal completion layout, recurring full constructions there can be tested as metatext about copying or completion rather than the medical or astronomical subject. Current section endings and last written lines are not sufficient evidence.

design.mechanism: A workshop closes separately produced booklets with a conventional statement about the completed unit, scribe or work.
design.unit: Physically independent completed booklet with externally established original ending, full terminal construction and all other occurrences of that construction.
design.contrast: Production-completion metatext versus topic vocabulary, general paragraph closure and accidental present-binding endpoints.
design.prediction: One recurrent construction contains a stable frame and an independently bound variable work/scribe slot across completed units; the same frame at ordinary interior contexts must obey an explicit quoted/metatext role or contradict the narrow completion hypothesis.
design.scope: RAW proposal only. No completion panel or variable slot is presently bound; missing leaves and rebinding may remove capacity. This is not a permission to access f116v or reserves and does not translate any frequent ending as finis. GDT1155 and generic boundary effects provide no semantic support. Word profiles and full counterexamples mandatory before any lexical assignment.
